complexity.explanation: Binary search has logarithmic time complexity as it repeatedly divides the search interval in half. The best case occurs when the target is found at the middle element on the first try. Space complexity is O(1) for iterative implementation.

description.brief: An efficient searching algorithm that finds the position of a target value within a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.
detailed: • Best case:    O(1)   - target found at middle
• Average case: O(log n) - typical performance
• Worst case:   O(log n) - target not found or at ends
• Much faster than linear search for large datasets
• Can be implemented iteratively or recursively
• Best for static sorted data with frequent searches
• Linear Search: O(n) but works on unsorted data
• Ternary Search: O(log n) but with more comparisons
• Interpolation Search: O(log log n) average but O(n) worst case
pseudocode: int binary_search(const std::vector<int>& arr, int target)
left = mid + 1;   // Search in right half
right = mid - 1;  // Search in left half
optimizations: Using (left + right) >>> 1 to prevent overflow in Java/C#
Using left + (right - left) / 2 to prevent overflow in C++
Early exit when target equals mid
Branch prediction optimization for predictable patterns
Vectorized binary search for SIMD processors
use_cases: Finding insertion point for new elements
disadvantages: Inefficient for small datasets (linear search may be better)
Poor performance on linked lists due to O(n) random access
Not suitable for dynamic data with frequent insertions/deletions
Overflow risk with naive mid calculation (left + right) / 2

variables.name: target
variables.description: The value being searched for in the array

variables.name: left
variables.description: Left boundary of the current search interval (inclusive)

variables.name: right
variables.description: Right boundary of the current search interval (inclusive)

variables.name: mid
variables.description: Middle index of the current search interval being examined

variables.name: mid_value
variables.description: Value at the middle index being compared with target

variables.name: comparisons
variables.description: Total number of comparisons performed so far

variables.name: search_interval_size
variables.description: Current size of the search interval (right - left + 1)

variables.name: found
variables.description: Whether the target has been found

variables.name: result_index
variables.description: Index where target was found, or -1 if not found

step_types.name: Loop Start
step_types.description: Beginning of a new search iteration

step_types.name: Mid Calculation
step_types.description: Calculating the middle index of current search interval

step_types.name: Compare Equal
step_types.description: Comparing middle value with target (equality check)

step_types.name: Compare Less
step_types.description: Checking if middle value is less than target

step_types.name: Compare Greater
step_types.description: Checking if middle value is greater than target

step_types.name: Found
step_types.description: Target value found at current mid index

step_types.name: Search Left
step_types.description: Moving search to left half (target is smaller)

step_types.name: Search Right
step_types.description: Moving search to right half (target is larger)

step_types.name: Not Found
